method: Instruction listings decoded directly from the PE bytes of the identified executable through its section table, with the executable size and SHA-256 verified first. Call and jump targets were enumerated by scanning the .text section for rel32 call and jmp instructions, so virtual and indirect callers are not covered. Addresses are absolute virtual addresses. No decompiled body is a tracked evidence dependency.
scope: Runtime state behind the DesktopWidget target cursor natives: the cursor state object, the current cursor fields, cursor creation and replacement, current-cursor selection, the range check and its failure path, the fresh cursor layout, the empty identity, the _getTargetCharacter result test and the _setTargetCursorImage side effects. Lua argument and return types are recorded in manifests/boot_native_call_contract.json and are not repeated. Client-side state does not establish server behavior.

tierVocabulary.STATIC: Read directly from instructions at the cited addresses.
tierVocabulary.INFERRED: A name or role assigned from the surrounding instructions. The bytes do not state it.

stateObject.accessor: 0x004D7310 returns the dword at +0x4C0 of its receiver. Each cursor entry point resolves the state object through it before using the vector or +0xB4 and +0xB8. 0x0075F060, 0x0075B6C0, 0x0075B700 and the other 0x0075F... thunks apply it to the dword stored at the start of their receiver. 0x00777F50 is entered with the state object already in ecx. 0x00562D30 is a method on the state object reached after the resolution in 0x0075B6C0 and 0x0075B700. The Lua callbacks load the worker receiver by reading the dword at the address 0x00CC7510 returns, then the dword at +0x04 of that value, then the dword at +0x04 of that value.

fields.role: Cursor vector. First pointer at +0xA8 and end pointer at +0xAC, with 4-byte entries that point at cursor objects. Size is (end - first) >> 2.
Current cursor index. 0xFFFFFFFF means none. The value _getCurrentTargetCursor reads before adding 1.

stateObject.currentIdentityReader: 0x0075B6A0 returns the dword at +0x04 of the current cursor, or 0xC0000000 when +0xB4 is 0. No Lua native among the cursor natives reaches it.

preInitValue.note: No store of +0xB4 or +0xB8 in the cursor workers other than the three reset sites. The construction of the state object and the value of both fields before the first _initTargetCursors call were not traced.

freshFields.role: Target identity. 0xC0000000 is the empty identity, -0x40000000 as a signed dword.
Targetable distance. 0x0055EB30 stores its float argument here.

freshFields.value: child objects of 0xAC bytes built through 0x0055E910
freshFields.role: Presentation children. 0x005623E0 and 0x00563510 act on them.
Image value. 0x005623E0 stores its argument here.

targetSetter.claim: The receiver of 0x0055E7A0 is the indexed cursor: 0x00562D30 loads the vector entry at 0x00562D94 and calls it at 0x00562E16. 0x0055E7A0 stores 0x004D6750 of the new target object (the dword at target +0x88) at +0x04 and the object at +0x0C. A null target stores 0xC0000000 at +0x04 and 0 at +0x0C. The same value as the stored object is a no-op. 0x0055EB30 is applied to the indexed cursor by 0x0075F010 at 0x0075F04E and stores its float argument at +0x10. The role names for +0x0C and +0x10 stay INFERRED.

facts.claim: _initTargetCursors stores the count at DesktopWidget +0x68 and then calls worker 0x0075EE70. The worker always writes +0xB4 = 0 and +0xB8 = 0xFFFFFFFF after its creation loop, on every call and for every count, including a count of 0 or below that skips the loop. The two stores precede the 8-byte event post and the byte store at +0x04 of the worker receiver.

The creation loop allocates 0x24 bytes through 0x009D1B35, constructs it through 0x00564B50 and stores it at index i through 0x00565D30 with the select flag 0. The select path of 0x00565D30 runs only for a nonzero flag, so the loop never selects a cursor. 0x00565D30 grows the vector through 0x007A0A10 only when its size is at most the index, so the vector size becomes the larger of its old size and the count and never shrinks. The loop discards the previous pointer 0x00565D30 returns and calls no release. Indices at or above a smaller new count keep their old cursor objects.

_setCurrentTargetCursor passes its argument minus 1 to 0x0075F060, which jumps to worker 0x00777F50. The worker tests the signed index. A negative index stores +0xB4 = 0 and +0xB8 = 0xFFFFFFFF, which is no cursor selected. A nonnegative index must be below the vector size by an unsigned compare and a vector whose first pointer is null fails that test for every index. An index in range stores the vector entry at +0xB4 and the index at +0xB8. A Lua number of 0 or below therefore selects none, a number from 1 up to the vector size selects that cursor and a larger number takes the failure path.

The worker posts the 8-byte event {1, 0xC0000000} through 0x004D7980 when the stored +0xB8 is nonzero, which includes the none value. It posts nothing when cursor index 0 is selected. _initTargetCursors posts the same event on every call. The event consumers were not traced.

The failure address 0x009D22B4 calls 0x009D2290 with five zero arguments. 0x009D2290 loads a handler through the pointer cell at 0x01363F1C and 0x009DF187. A nonzero handler is jumped to. Otherwise the routine calls 0x009DF94A with argument 2 and then jumps to 0x009D2194, which builds an exception record with code 0xC000000D, calls UnhandledExceptionFilter and then TerminateProcess with that code. Whether the pointer cell holds a handler at run time and what the 0x009DF94A call does (for example a terminate mode or an error report) were not traced and are unknown.

0x009D2290 is the C runtime invalid-parameter routine and 0x009D22B4 is its no-argument wrapper, the form a checked vector subscript calls. The bytes show the shape. The routine name is an identification.

Every cursor worker that takes a cursor index tests it against the vector size and takes the failure path at 0x009D22B4 outside it. The size is the vector size, not the count stored at DesktopWidget +0x68. The workers are 0x0075EFC0 for the image, 0x0075F010 for the distance, 0x00562D30 for the target character setter and clear reached through 0x0075B6C0 and 0x0075B700, 0x0075F0E0 for the target identity reader and the worker 0x00777F50. 0x0075F070 loops over the vector size and tests each entry the same way. The target character setter 0x0075B6C0 first resolves the identity through 0x004D9970 and does nothing when that returns null.

A cursor constructed by 0x00564B50 holds 0xC0000000 at +0x04 and no later store in the constructor body changes it. 0x0075F0E0 returns the dword at +0x04 of the indexed cursor. _getTargetCharacter compares that value with 0xC0000000 and pushes Nil on equality. A fresh cursor therefore reads Nil.

For a non-empty identity _getTargetCharacter converts it through 0x00CC9320 and resolves a control through 0x00CC7A50. A null control pushes Nil. A control whose byte at +0x5C is zero pushes Nil. Any other control is pushed through 0x00748B30.
The meaning of the control byte at +0x5C and the writers that set it were not traced.

_setAllTargetCursorMask passes its flag to 0x0075F070, which calls 0x00563510 on every vector entry that is not null. 0x00563510 writes the flag byte to +0x8C of the two child objects at cursor +0x18 and +0x1C and of the objects held in the globals 0x0133728C and 0x01337290, and calls 0x00562E90 on each. The flag is not stored on the state object. A child constructed by 0x0055E910 starts with +0x8C = 0, so a cursor's own two children are unmasked at creation. 0x00562E90 reads +0x8C of its own receiver.

Each direct call or jump to the workers comes from one place. 0x0075EE70 from 0x006E5028, 0x00777F50 from 0x0075F069, 0x0075F060 from 0x006E532B and 0x00564B50 from 0x0075EECC. A teardown loop at 0x0075EF40 clears every entry through 0x00565D30 with a null object and is called from 0x0057828E only, which is not a cursor native.

The two globals 0x0133728C and 0x01337290 are shared by all cursors. The cursor constructor creates them only while the refcount at 0x01337288 is 0, stores them, and increments the refcount at 0x00564D50. The release path at 0x0055EAC9 decrements the refcount and, when it reaches 0, deletes and nulls both globals, so the next construction recreates them with +0x8C = 0. The globals therefore keep the mask flag written by 0x00563510 across later cursor creation while any earlier cursor survives. The references to 0x01337288 were found by scanning and the callers of the release path were not traced.

Whether a cursor's drawing path consults the shared globals, and so whether a cursor created after a mask call is observably masked, was not traced, and the locators are read sites of the globals found by a reference scan. Because the globals retain the flag (TC-13), a host-wide mask flag that survives later cursor creation may match the client more closely than a mask that is not retained.

rows.behavior: Reads +0xB8 at 0x0075B697 and pushes it plus 1 through 0x00584F70, so none reads as 0 and a selected index i reads as i + 1.

image.claim: The callback reads two ints, passes argument 0 minus 1 and argument 1 to 0x0075EFC0 and returns. 0x0075EFC0 range-checks the index, then 0x005623E0 stores the image value at cursor +0x20 and calls 0x00561F10 with it on the objects at cursor +0x18 and +0x1C.

cursorOneBranch.claim: After the store the callback continues only when the zero-based index is 0 and the byte at DesktopWidget +0x7C is 0. It builds an identity from the widget through 0x00CC73B0 and tests it with 0x00CC7BE0 using the immediate 0x0007A124 and -1. When the test passes and DesktopWidget +0x70 equals the dword at 0x0130C778, it reads the identity of cursor 0 through 0x0075F0E0, calls 0x0075D460, posts a message through 0x0075EB30 and stores a value derived from the widget identity through 0x00CC9320 at +0x70. When the test fails and +0x70 differs from the dword at 0x0130C778, it reads the identity of cursor 0, calls 0x0075D460, posts the message with the dword at 0x0130C778 as one payload value and stores that dword at +0x70. Otherwise it returns.

predicate.claim: 0x00CC7BE0 looks the identity up through 0x00CD8160 and returns false when the lookup is null, when the record byte at +0x7D is 0 or when the record dword at +0x14 is 0. Otherwise it calls 0x00CE53D0 on the object 0x00CEB490 returns for the object held at +0x214 of the engine, with the immediate and -1, and returns its result. What the immediate selects and what 0x00CE53D0 tests were not traced.

message.claim: 0x0075EB30 fills a 0x18-byte message with code 0xCD and sends it through 0x004D6D10 with the two identities it receives as its second and third arguments. The message consumer was not traced.

widgetFields.claim: The DesktopWidget constructor 0x006E0650 sets +0x68 = 0, +0x6C = 0, +0x74 = 0.0f, +0x78 = 0, +0x79 = 1 and +0x7A, +0x7B, +0x7C = 0, and initializes the +0x70 identity through 0x00CC9310. The byte at +0x7C is stored 1 at 0x006FEA1E and 0x006FEC6C inside DesktopWidget methods that compare +0x68 with an index plus 1, and is stored from a register at 0x006FEAE4 and 0x006FED32. The method at 0x006FE960 has one direct caller at 0x008A3EB3. The Lua natives that reach these methods were not traced.

sentinel.claim: The dword at 0x0130C778 holds 0xE0000000 in the image and is referenced at many call sites. The cursor-one branch compares +0x70 with it and stores it at +0x70 when the test fails. Its role as the no cached identity value is INFERRED.

remaining: The Lua natives that call the DesktopWidget methods writing +0x7C.
Whether the 0x0007A124 query returns the value of the work member mainTargetDecidedFlag (key 500004), which manifests/stub_overload_native_call_contract.json identifies.
The consumer of message code 0xCD and of the 0x0075D460 call.

open: The state object construction and the values of +0xB4 and +0xB8 before the first _initTargetCursors call.
The consumers of the 8-byte event posted through 0x004D7980.
The meaning of the control byte at +0x5C.
Whether the invalid-parameter handler cell at 0x01363F1C holds a handler at run time.
The fields at cursor +0x14 and the roles of the child objects at +0x18 and +0x1C.
The Lua natives that write DesktopWidget +0x7C.
Whether the cursor drawing path consults the shared globals at 0x0133728C and 0x01337290.
The effect of the 0x009DF94A call with argument 2 on the failure path.
boundaries: These are client-side static observations. No retail client run or live Lua call supports them.
Callers were enumerated only for direct call and jmp instructions in the .text section.
Role names marked INFERRED come from the surrounding instructions and are not named by the client.
The contracts do not establish server behavior.
